title: Libya sanctions amended: new offence of receiving frozen Libyan funds
summary: From 16 December 2026, it is an offence under the Libya sanctions to receive frozen funds of a designated person in response to a payment request. The changes also add a targeted arms embargo and new grounds for designation.
what_changes: It is an offence to receive frozen funds of a designated person in response to a payment request, if the receiver knows or suspects their source.
The explanatory note says this covers funds of the Libyan Investment Authority and the Libyan Africa Investment Portfolio.
A new power allows designations for a targeted arms embargo covering goods, technology, technical assistance, finance and brokering.
New designation grounds include illicitly exporting crude oil, refined petroleum products or other natural resources from Libya.
who_it_applies_to: All UK law firms, as UK persons bound by the Libya sanctions, especially firms that may receive payments linked to Libyan state investment bodies.

history.event: Regulations made on 24 November 2026 and in force from 16 December 2026.
